instruction.text: This diagram shows the top of Anglo-Saxon society. Select the word bretwalda to learn more about him.
instruction.sound: This diagram shows the top of Anglo-Saxon society. Select the word bretwalder to learn more about him.

atoms.b: Britain was split into several different ((++kingdoms planets)), each ruled by its own king.
atoms.sound: Britain was split into several different kingdoms, each ruled by its own king.

atoms.b: Sometimes, there would also be a bretwalda, or “Britain-ruler”, who was a ((++king servant)) of kings.
atoms.sound: Sometimes, there would also be a bretwalder, or “Britain-ruler”, who was a king of kings.

instruction.text: Drag the coin into the purse.

finish.sound: A bretwalder had enough power and organisation to reintroduce coins. This is one of the coins of Ethel-stan, the first ever King of England!
text: A bretwalda had enough power and organisation to reintroduce coins. This is one of the coins of Aethelstan, the first ever King of England!

instruction.text: Select the word aethelings to learn more about them.
instruction.sound: Select the word ethellings to learn more about them.

atoms.b: Aethelings were the ((++male ghost)) relatives of kings.
atoms.sound: Ethellings were the male relatives of kings.

atoms.b: They were supposed to help run the ((++kingdom business)), but sometimes they tried to take the ((++throne sofa)) for themselves — even by killing the king!
atoms.sound: They were supposed to help run the kingdom, but sometimes they tried to take the throne for themselves — even by killing the king!
